title: OST for my upcoming tetris-y roguelite, Astromino - made with Udio & some light editing
author: BenMakesGames
selftext:
I've got 20ish years of SE experience, and have occasionally acted as BA, PM, and/or SCRUM master as the situation warranted. having that background, it's been simultaneously weird but cool to go from coding all the time for work and for fun to coding almost none. "but I'm a dev! is this really okay?!" -> "but I am also a BA/PM when the situation calls... and the situation is calling!"

I started making Astromino with the thought "how far can I get if I put on my BA/PM hat, write tickets, and be hands-off with the coding?" probably to no surprise to a lot of devs (especially here), the answer is "very far" :P

I think having an SE background, ideally from a few different jobs, helps a lot. knowing what's made some dev departments awesome or less awesome lets me be the "dev department of my dreams". I trust my dev (most places I've worked are good at this); ask my dev what tech stack it would feel most comfortable using to build the thing I want (tech stack is non-negotiable at most places I've worked); ask my dev to identify tech debt, and give it time to address it! (have you worked a place that actually spent time on tech debt? I haven't! :P)

it's also been funny to REALLY come to appreciate the position my BAs at larger companies have always been in, asking "stupid" questions about a code base they don't understand... because now I'm in that same position, asking those same stupid questions! but it's fine: my dev is knowledgeable, pleasant to work with, fast, makes mistakes sometimes, sure, but so have I always done, and I know the processes to help minimize & catch such mistakes.

---

if you're looking for music for your game, I've been enjoying Suno. whenever I got bored writing and implementing tickets for Astromino, it was dangerously easy to waste an hour generating and listening to a few songs to find a new one to throw into the game's playlist :P I finally made myself stop - this is the result.
